blogs.title: How to Choose the Right Logo Print Method
blogs.excerpt: Screen, DTF, sublimation or embroidery? A quick guide to picking the right method for each product.
body: Screen printing is best for large runs with one or two colours. It is durable and cost-effective for T-shirts and tote bags.
DTF handles full-colour logos and photos on cotton and blends without minimum colour limits. Embroidery gives a premium feel on polos and caps.
Not sure? Send your logo and we will suggest the best method and show a free preview before printing.

blogs.title: 5 Branded Items That Actually Get Used
blogs.excerpt: Not every giveaway works. These five keep your logo in front of people every single day.
body: Mugs, pens, bottles, diaries and T-shirts top the list because people use them daily at work or home.
Choose quality over quantity. A well-made bottle is kept for years while a cheap giveaway is thrown away.
Match the item to your audience: staff get uniforms, clients get diaries and bottles, event guests get tote bags and pens.

blogs.title: ID Cards and Lanyards: What Every Office Needs
blogs.excerpt: Photo ID cards improve security and make your team look professional. Here is how to order them right.
body: Collect employee names, designations, IDs and photos in one spreadsheet. Clean photos with plain backgrounds print best.
Match lanyard colours to your brand and add a retractable holder if staff swipe cards at doors.
Order a few extra cards for new joiners so onboarding is smooth.
